implication: Regulation 31(4) filings trigger acquirer-side disclosure obligations within two days of crossing thresholds; the filing confirms a material event but does not disclose the acquisition quantum or consideration-those details appear in the full Form A or supplementary SAST disclosures, which require cross-referencing with the company's investor portal for deal specifics.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 – Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: central - mandatory disclosure by acquirer within 2 days of crossing threshold; triggers public announcement and regulatory approval pathways.

framework.ref: SEBI Takeover Regulations 2011 – Regulations 3–6 (acquirer definition & threshold events)
framework.note: central - defines 'acquirer', materiality thresholds (5%, 10%, etc.), and acquisition modes (direct purchase, open offer, preferential allotment).

framework.ref: SEBI Takeover Regulations 2011 – Regulation 10 (open offer obligation)
framework.note: central - if threshold crossed, may trigger 20% open offer to minority shareholders at floor price.
procedural - governs exemptions (e.g. inter-se transfer, rights issue, preferential allotment subject to FIPB/Audit Committee approval).

framework.ref: Companies Act 2013 – Section 117A (Board approval for preferential allotment)
framework.note: procedural - if shares issued post-takeover, requires board & shareholder approval with 3/4 majority.
procedural - if acquirer appoints nominee directors post-crossing 25%, may require disclosure of director appointments.
procedural - issuer must announce material acquisition/takeover event to exchanges within 30 minutes (or in case of pricing details, within 24 hours).

framework.ref: SEBI Takeover Regulations 2011 – Regulation 14 (pricing formula for open offer)
framework.note: procedural - if open offer triggered, floor price determined by highest of (a) 30-day/60-day VWAP, or (b) last negotiated price, or (c) CCI/SEBI approval price.

parties: Mahendra Kumar Daga; Orient Bell Limited
headline: Mahendra Kumar Daga files Regulation 31(4) disclosure under SEBI Takeover Code with NSE
sum: Promoter Mahendra Kumar Daga submitted a mandatory Regulation 31(4) disclosure to NSE under the SEBI Takeover Regulations 2011, signalling a substantial acquisition event or related shareholding change in Orient Bell Limited (ceramics & sanitaryware manufacturer).
detail: Mahendra Kumar Daga, a promoter/substantial shareholder of Orient Bell Limited (BSE: 500093; NSE: ORIENTBELL), filed a Regulation 31(4) disclosure with NSE. This regulation requires acquirers to file within 48 hours of crossing 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, 80%, 90% or 95% shareholding thresholds. The disclosure was submitted via the NSE archives system on or around 22 June 2026. The filing itself does not provide the acquisition price, number of shares acquired, or resulting shareholding percentage in the headline; those are contained in the detailed Form A or subsequent SAST (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) schedules.

triggers.law: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations 2011 – Regulation 31(4)
triggers.note: Disclosure event trigger: acquirer must file within 2 days of crossing any prescribed shareholding threshold (5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 95%).
If 20%+ threshold crossed, triggers mandatory open offer to minority shareholders (unless exempt under Regulation 16).
Issuer (Orient Bell) must separately announce material acquisition event to exchanges within 30 minutes of knowledge.
